title: CrossRAT_Incident_Response_05e
description: You are an incident responder tasked with investigating and responding to a CrossRAT malware infection. CrossRAT is a backdoor tool capable of targeting Windows, OSX, and Linux systems, allowing attackers to exfiltrate data and maintain persistence. Your goal is to identify the infection, understand its behavior, and contain the threat.

levels.title: Introduction
levels.content: You are an incident responder tasked with investigating and responding to a CrossRAT malware infection. CrossRAT is a backdoor tool capable of targeting Windows, OSX, and Linux systems, allowing attackers to exfiltrate data and maintain persistence. Your goal is to identify the infection, understand its behavior, and contain the threat.

levels.title: Get Access
levels.cloud_content: Access the target host via SSH using the following credentials: Username: cyrano, Password: cyrano. Enter 'start' to begin.
levels.local_content: Access the target host via SSH using the following credentials: Username: cyrano, Password: cyrano. Enter 'start' to begin.

levels.title: Suspicious Service Discovery
levels.content: While monitoring the network, you noticed unusual outbound connections from the target host. Investigate the target host to identify any unauthorized or suspicious services running. The suspicious service 'mediamgrs.jar.service' should be discoverable through the described methods.
levels.solution: To identify suspicious services, you can use the `systemctl list-units --type=service` command to list all running services. Look for any services that seem out of place or unfamiliar. Additionally, you can use the `netstat -tuln` command to check for any suspicious network connections.

hints.title: First hint title
hints.content: Check the list of running services and look for any that seem out of place or unfamiliar.

hints.title: Second hint title
hints.content: Use the `systemctl list-units --type=service` command to list all running services.

hints.title: Third hint title
hints.content: Look for services with unusual names or those that are not part of standard system services.

levels.title: Persistence Discovery
levels.content: You have identified a suspicious service. Determine how this service is automatically started after a system reboot. The persistence mechanism 'payload-transfer.timer' should be discoverable through the described methods.
levels.solution: To identify persistence mechanisms, you can use the `systemctl list-unit-files --state=enabled` command to list all enabled systemd services. Additionally, you can check for any cron jobs or scheduled tasks using the `crontab -l` command.

hints.title: First hint title
hints.content: Investigate systemd services and timers to find how the suspicious service is maintained.

hints.title: Second hint title
hints.content: Use the `systemctl list-unit-files --state=enabled` command to list all enabled systemd services.

hints.title: Third hint title
hints.content: Look for timers or services that might be responsible for restarting the suspicious service.

levels.title: C2 Communication Discovery (Port)
levels.content: Analyze the network traffic to determine which port is used for the suspicious communication between the target host and the potential command-and-control server. The port '2223' should be discoverable through the described methods.
levels.solution: To identify the port used for C2 communication, you can use the `netstat -tuln` command to list all network connections. Look for any suspicious connections to external IPs or unusual ports.

hints.title: First hint title
hints.content: Check the network connections and listen ports to find the one used by the suspicious service.

hints.title: Second hint title
hints.content: Use the `netstat -tuln` command to list all network connections.

hints.title: Third hint title
hints.content: Look for connections to external IPs or unusual ports that might indicate C2 communication.
